sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page yuga1244 and reference record 556571 (Mathews 1902, hh:typ:Mathews:Yookumbill).

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1903. The Murawarri and other Australian languages. Queensland Geographical Journal 18 (in the same archive.org scanned volume as above).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Yookumbill only as the representative type of inland NSW languages; no Yugambal phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1902. Languages of some native tribes of Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria. Journal and Proceedings of the Royal Society of New South Wales 36: 135-190.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only footnote cross-references to 'my Yookumbil Language, Queensland Geographical Journal'; no Yugambal material (covers Pikumbil = Bigambal, Yualeai, etc.).

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1901-02. The Thoorga Language [with Appendix: The Yookumbill Language, pp. 63-67]. Queensland Geographical Journal 17: 49-73.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only an orthographic convention, in the Thoorga part (p. 50): 'The accent is shown thus, Kul'la, and when two syllables are accented, both are marked in the same way.' The Yookumbill appendix (pp. 63-67) has no phonology section of its own; it carries accent marks on cited words (Bun'dar, gib'beer, uk'keether, woo'nar, mee'kai, gir'ri, goo'pee, boo'roo, ngoo'ra, bur'gan, koo'nee, ing'gal) - all first-syllable except the language name Yoo-kum'-bill / U-kum'-bil - but states no rule of stress placement.
